newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Stals sees SAfrica GDP around two pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Stals sees SAfrica GDP around two pct in 1997.

text.p: South African Reserve Board Governor Christian Stals said growth this year should slow down to around a two percent expansion in Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
Stals told reporters at the World Economic Forum that growth should pick up again in 1998.
"GDP was about a three and half percent increase last year and already slowed down in the second half. We are talking this year of about a two percent increase in GDP," Stals said.
A December survey of 27 South African economists showed they saw 1997 GDP growth slowing to between two and 2.2 percent.
Stals said lower growth, lower imports and a declining current accounts deficit were relieving exchange rate pressure on the rand.
"The rand has gotten more stable in the past months. We have weathered the currency storm of last year," Stals said.
